params.name: page
params.description:
The page number for [paginated results](/products/payments-odl/api-docs/ripplenet/best-practices/pagination/). The value is zero-based, where `0` represents the first page.
Set it to `0` to get the first page of results.

params.name: size
params.description: Number of payments to return per page.

params.name: sending_host
params.description: Optional parameter for filtering `with sendingHost` value.

params.name: receiving_host
params.description: Optional parameter for filtering with `receivingHost` value.

params.name: sending_account
params.description: Optional parameter for filtering with `sendingAccount` value.

params.name: receiving_account
params.description: Optional parameter for filtering with `receivingAccount` value.

params.name: sending_currency
params.description: Optional parameter for filtering with `sendingCurrency` value.

params.name: receiving_currency
params.description: Optional parameter for filtering with `receivingCurrency` value.

params.name: payment_id
params.description: Optional parameter for filtering with `paymentId` value. This parameter is deprecated. Please use `payment_ids` instead

params.name: payment_type
params.description: Filters for payments based on the type of payment. Valid types are `REGULAR`, `RETURN`.

params.name: internal_id
params.description: Optional parameter for filtering with internalId.

params.name: sender_end_to_end_id
params.description: Optional parameter for filtering with senderEndToEndId.

params.name: connector_role
params.description: Filters for payments based on the role of the responding connector. Valid roles are `SENDING`, `INTERMEDIARY`, `RECEIVING`, and `INTERNAL`. The `INTERNAL` role is meant for payments between RippleNet Cloud and RippleNet where the sender and receiver accounts are on the same RippleNet instance. Use role with state to find payments waiting on action from you as the sending or receiving (or internal) connector.

params.name: state
params.description: Deprecated, should use states parameter. Returns payments in the specified state. The following options are valid: `ACCEPTED`, `COMPLETED`, `EXECUTED`, `FAILED`, `LOCKED`, `LOCK_DECLINED`, `PREPARED`, `RETURNED`, and `SETTLEMENT_DECLINED`

params.name: states
params.description: Returns payments in the specified states. The following options are valid: `ACCEPTED`, `COMPLETED`, `EXECUTED`, `FAILED`, `LOCKED`, `LOCK_DECLINED`, `PREPARED`, `RETURNED`, and `SETTLEMENT_DECLINED`

params.name: before
params.description: Filters for payments where the payments `range_field` column value is before this specified time stamp (not inclusive). You can also specify `after` to create a time range between `after` and `before`. If before is specified, `range_field` must also be specified.

params.name: after
params.description: Filters for payments where the payments `range_field` column value is after this specified time stamp (not inclusive). You can also specify `before` to create a time range between `after` and `before`. If `after` is specified, `range_field` must also be specified.

params.name: range_field
params.description: Designates the column name of the payments database table that is used for filtering payments before/after/between time stamps. The following options are valid: `CREATED_AT`, `MODIFIED_AT`, `ACCEPTED_AT`, `LOCKED_AT`, `EXECUTED_AT`, `COMPLETED_AT`, `RETURNED_AT` and `EXPIRES_AT`. For example, if you specify `range_field`=`MODIFIED_AT`, you would specify a time stamp (in the 24 character ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ format used in payment objects) as the value for `before` and/or `after` to fetch payments before, after, or between the specified time range(s) (not inclusive). If `range_field` is specified, `before` and/or `after` must also be specified.

params.name: amount_range_field
params.description: Designates the column name of the payments database table that is used for filtering payments greater/less/between amounts. For example, if you specify `amount_range_field=SENDING_AMOUNT`, you would specify an amount as the value for `greater` and/or `less` to fetch payments greater, less, or between the specified amounts (inclusive). If `amount_range_field` is specified, `minAmount` and/or `maxAmount` must also be specified.

params.name: min_amount
params.description: Optional parameter for filtering with min sending/receiving amount.

params.name: max_amount
params.description: Optional parameter for filtering with max sending/receiving amount.

params.name: with_labels
params.description:
Returns payments with the specified labels.

If you apply `with_labels` with multiple labels, the response returns payments with at least one of the specified labels.

For example, the query,

?with_labels=string1,string2

returns payments with either "string1" OR "string2".

params.name: without_labels
params.description:
Returns payments that do not have any of the specified labels.

If you apply `without_labels` with multiple labels, the response returns payments that do not have any of the specified labels.

For example, the query,

?without_labels=string3,string4

returns payments that are not labeled with either "string3" OR "string4".

If you apply both `with_labels` and `without_labels` parameters, the response returns payments that have at least one of the specified `with_labels` strings but omits payments that also have any of the the `without_labels` strings.

For example, the query,

?with_labels=string1&without_labels=string3

returns payments with "string1" but not payments with "string3".

params.name: sort_field
params.description: Sorts results according to the specified field. Valid options are `PAYMENT_ID`, `EXPIRES_AT`, `MODIFIED_AT` and `CREATED_AT`.

params.name: sort_direction
params.description: Sorts result according to the specified direction. Valid options are `ASC`, `DESC`.

params.name: load_additional_details
params.description: This parameter can be used to exclude additional info being returned for each payment object. Additional info which will be excluded if the flag set to false include user_info, ripplenet_info, execution_results and internal_info.labels

params.name: payment_ids
params.description: List of paymentIds to search for

items.docs: Retrieves all payments in an instance of xCurrent that meet the criteria defined by the query parameters. You can use the query parameters to filter payments. The default parameters are `sort_field : MODIFIED_AT` , `sort_direction : DESC` , `page : 0` , `size : 10`

params.description: Unique identifier of the payment to return to `ACCEPTED` state.

items.docs: Returns a rejected payment from the `LOCK_DECLINED` state to the `ACCEPTED` state. The payment sender must include repaired [user_info](/products/payments-odl/api-docs/ripplenet/resources/srpo/user-info) in the request body.

params.name: payment_id
params.description: Unique identifier of the payment to fail.

items.docs:
Fails a payment. Fail payment is a deliberate action that permanently stops the payment and puts it into a non-recoverable state.

An institution _rejects_ a payment to solicit changes to [user_info](/products/payments-odl/api-docs/ripplenet/resources/srpo/user-info); it _fails_ a payment to stop it altogether. The receiving institution can make this request multiple times to provide a log of each subsequent sub-state until it is ready to make the [Complete payment](#operation/completePayment) request.

All nodes on the payment chain can make this request multiple times to provide a log of each subsequent sub-state until the receiver is ready to make the [Complete payment](#operation/completePayment) request.

items.docs: Marks a payment as complete by placing it in the `COMPLETED` state. Typically, the receiving institution makes this request when it has delivered payment funds to the final beneficiary on its internal systems outside of xCurrent.
